statement: When $x^3+ax^2+bx+6$ is divided by $x-2$ the remainder is $0$, and when divided by $x-3$ the remainder is $8$. Find $a$ and $b$.
solution:
Let $f(x)=x^3+ax^2+bx+6$. By the remainder theorem, $f(2)=0$ and $f(3)=8$.

$f(2)=8+4a+2b+6=0$ gives $4a+2b=-14$, i.e. $2a+b=-7$.

$f(3)=27+9a+3b+6=8$ gives $9a+3b=-25$, i.e. $3a+b=-\tfrac{25}{3}$.

Subtracting the first equation from the second: $a=-\tfrac{25}{3}+7=-\tfrac{4}{3}$. Then $b=-7-2a=-7+\tfrac{8}{3}=-\tfrac{13}{3}$.

So $a=-\tfrac{4}{3}$ and $b=-\tfrac{13}{3}$.
hints: Use the remainder theorem: f(2)=0 and f(3)=8.
Write two linear equations in a and b.
